column3: NKJV has “perverting the nation,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “our nation.” “Tribute” is rendered “taxes.”
Close to the Greek; “You say it” is rendered “It is as you say.”
Close to the Greek; “guilt” is rendered “fault.”
Close to the Greek; “insisting” is rendered “the more fierce.”
NKJV has “heard of Galilee,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has only “having heard.”
NKJV has “heard many things,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “heard about Him.” “Sign” is rendered “miracle.”
Close to the Greek; “troops” is rendered “men of war.”
NKJV has “for I sent you back to him,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “for he sent Him back to us.”
This verse is absent from the critical text; NKJV includes it following the Textus Receptus (“it was necessary for him to release one to them at the feast”).
NKJV includes “and of the chief priests,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “their voices prevailed.”
